The user's direction follows. Attend to it carefully, and respond in exactly one of the two forms described above.

Combine the functionality of the two selected widgets so I can move it close to a sticky note and press a button to generate an image

reasoning:
The user wants to combine the two selected widgets: the closest note finder and the image generator. They want a widget that can be moved close to a sticky note and press a button to generate an image. Looking at the two widgets: 1. **fluid.demos.closestNoteFinder** - finds the closest sticky note to the widget's position, shows its text and distance. It has `closest` computed from `{tldrawHost}.notes` and `{self}.hostBounds`, `noteText`, `distance`. 2. **fluid.demos.imageGenerator** - has a text input for a prompt, and searches Pixabay for images, displaying results with credits. It has `state` with `prompt`, `isGenerating`, `error`, `images`, `index`, `refreshedId`. The combination: A widget that when a button is pressed, finds the closest sticky note (presumably the note it's near) and uses that note's text as the prompt to generate an image. Or shows the closest note and generates an image from it. The user says "move it close to a sticky note and press a button to generate an image". So the widget: sits on the canvas, can be moved near a note. The note's text is used as an image search prompt (or the closest note's text becomes the prompt). Pressing a button generates the image. Design: An umbrella layer `fluid.demos.noteImageGenerator` (or similar) that combines: - Shows the closest note's text/distance (from closestNoteFinder) - Uses the closest note's text as prompt for image generation - Has a button to generate Options for composition: per the strategy hints, "To compose two widgets, define a fresh 'umbrella' layer with `fluid.topLevelWidget` as the last of its `$layers`, holding each of them as a subcomponent... Choose the view of just one of them as the view of the umbrella with `view: "{first}.view"`, and cross-inject between them with references... If both widgets must remain visible, the umbrella may instead have a template of its own holding an `@id` element for each subcomponent." The image generator's prompt - we could wire the closest note's text into the image generator's `state.prompt`. A reference may override a single member of a widget's reactive state, e.g. `state: {prompt = "{first}.output"}`. So umbrella layer: ```js fluid.def("fluid.demos.noteToImage", { $layers: ["fluid.topLevelWidget", ...], // Actually per instructions: list the existing layer in $layers followed by fluid.topLevelWidget noteFinder: { $component: { $layers: "fluid.demos.closestNoteFinder" } }, imageGen: { $component: { $layers: "fluid.demos.imageGenerator", state: { prompt: "{noteFinder}.noteText" // or maybe keep prompt but default it } } }, view: "{imageGen}.view" }); ``` Wait, but the image generator's view template has its own input field where the user can still type. The prompt would be overridden by the closest note's text. Hmm, but `{noteFinder}.noteText` is a reference; writing through it writes to the original site... but here we want it to override. Actually the precedence: subcomponent layer merges with user... the `state` in the `$component` record is at `subcomponent` precedence which is weaker than `user` but stronger than `dynamicLayers`. Hmm. Since `state` is a `$reactiveRoot`, the value is computed... Actually `state` is `$reactiveRoot: {prompt: "", ...}`. If we override `prompt` with a reference, the subcomponent's state gets prompt set to the closest note's text. But actually, maybe simpler and more robust: create the new widget fresh with templates? The instructions favor reusing layers. Let me think. Option A: Umbrella composing both: ```js fluid.def("fluid.demos.noteImageGen", { $layers: ["fluid.demos.closestNoteFinder", "fluid.demos.imageGenerator", "fluid.topLevelWidget"], preferredSize: {w: 400, h: 640}, noteFinder parts merged from both parents... ``` Hmm, this is getting complicated. When two layers both derive... Let me think about merging. If the umbrella lists both as parent layers, the members `closest`, `noteText`, `distance`, etc. from closestNoteFinder and `state`, `image`, methods, subcomponents (`errorMessage`, `loadingMessage`, `result`) from imageGenerator all merge. Then `state.prompt = "{self}.noteText"`? But wait, `prompt` needs `{noteText}`... `noteText` is `{self}.closest.text`, which works: it shows the closest note's text ("A red fox in the snow") or a message like "No sticky notes found". Hmm, but if not placed near a note, the text would be "Not placed on a canvas" or "No sticky notes found" — not ideal prompts. Maybe fall back to prompting. But the user's direction: "move it close to a sticky note and press a button to generate an image". The button is the generator's "Find Image" button which uses `state.prompt`. Actually the image generator's template has the input field showing the prompt and the button. If we bind prompt to noteText, the user can see what search will happen. That's good. Also the closestNoteFinder has `distanceLine` subcomponent displaying distance. The finder's template shows title, noteText, and the distance line. Combined with the imageGen view... The finder's view (SFC template) vs imageGen's view (SFC template). We can only pick one view for the umbrella unless we make a custom template with @id elements for subcomponents. Better: umbrella with its own template (via `fluid.templateViewComponent`) with sections: a finder section showing closest note text/distance, and the image gen section with input, buttons, messages, result. Use `@id="errorMessage"` etc. But that duplicates the styles... hmm, styles are injected globally from SFCs when loaded, so the CSS classes from both SFCs are available. We can write a template using those classes. Wait — but subcomponents: the umbrella as `fluid.topLevelWidget` — does it have a `view` directive support? Yes, SFC adds view; or we can write `view: {$component: {$layers: "fluid.templateViewComponent", template: "..."}}`. Let me design the new layer: ```js fluid.def("fluid.demos.nearbyImageGenerator", { $layers: ["fluid.topLevelWidget"], preferredSize: {w: 400, h: 640}, // members merged from a finder subcomponent closest: "$compute:fluid.demos.closestNoteFinder.findClosest({tldrawHost}.notes, {self}.hostBounds)", noteText: "{self}.closest.text", distance: "{self}.closest.distance", state: { $reactiveRoot: { isGenerating: false, error: "", images: [], index: 0, refreshedId: null } }, // computed members copied from imageGenerator layer... image: "$compute:fluid.demos.imageGenerator.currentImage({self}.state.images, {self}.state.index)", cannotGenerate: "$compute:fluid.demos.imageGenerator.cannotGenerate({self}.noteText, {self}.state.isGenerating)", cannotShowAnother: ..., buttonLabel: ..., errorMessage: {...}, loadingMessage: {...}, result: {...}, keyDown: ..., generate: {func: "fluid.demos.imageGenerator.generate", args: ["{self}.state"]}, ... view: ... }); ``` Hmm but that copies a lot. The strategy hints say to prefer composition of fresh "umbrella" layer with subcomponents over redefining/copying. But the merged-parents approach does reuse the existing layers wholesale — it lists them as parents and inherits their members. That is actually quite clean and idiomatic in this framework: "redefined... with fluid.topLevelWidget as the last of its $layers". Hmm, but careful: both parents have `view` via SFC loader (fluid.sfcTemplateViewComponent with their own templates). The umbrella's own view must be defined to combine. If the umbrella defines `view`, it overrides both parents' views (since it's listed later, it beats them). Good. Also `preferredSize` conflicts? closestNoteFinder: 260x200, imageGenerator: 360x460. List closestNoteFinder first then imageGenerator then topLevelWidget, and set our own preferredSize 400x640 or so. Actually the umbrella's own `preferredSize` member beats both parents. Potential conflict: both layers define members with the same names? closestNoteFinder has: preferredSize, closest, noteText, distance, distanceLine. imageGenerator has: preferredSize, state, isGenerating, error, image, cannotGenerate, cannotShowAnother, buttonLabel, errorMessage, loadingMessage, result, keyDown, generate, showAnother, refresh. Only `preferredSize` overlaps, and the later one wins. No real conflict. The combined widget: - title "Closest Sticky Note & Image Generator" — or reuse template classes. - Show closest note text and distance (uses `{self}.noteText` and `{self}.distance`) - Image input: bind value to... We want the prompt to be the note text. If we do `value: "{self}.noteText"` — but then reading back would try to write to `closest.text` which is a computed value (not writable) — actually `closest` is `$compute`, so write-back is read-only, attribute re-materialised from element state. But the note text is also used directly for generating... The generator button uses `state.prompt`... we set the input to noteText but `cannotGenerate` and `generate` use `state.prompt`. Alternative: make `state.prompt` itself track the note text. Since `state` is a `$reactiveRoot`, and its `prompt` field... we could define in the umbrella a `$compute` for prompt and override `state.prompt`? Hmm, `$reactiveRoot` with value being an object; prompt is a primitive. If we override `state.prompt` with `{self}.noteText` (a reference), precedence: umbrella's layer beats parents, so state.prompt becomes a reference to noteText. But `$reactiveRoot` merging: the umbrella's `state` replaces the parents' `state` wholesale (primitive? it's a signal record with $reactiveRoot key). The umbrella defines its own `state` `{$reactiveRoot: {isGenerating: false, ...}}` (excluding prompt) plus a separate `prompt`? Hmm wait — careful: the umbrella's `state` value replaces the parents' `state` entirely because it's a signal record (replaced as a unit). Then `prompt` wouldn't be in state. Then we have member `prompt: "{self}.noteText"`? But the existing subcomponents (errorMessage etc.) and computeds reference `state.prompt`... wait no — `cannotGenerate` uses `{self}.state.prompt`, `generate` uses state passed directly. We could keep `state` as the umbrella's own `$reactiveRoot` with prompt initially from note: can't express "initial value as reference" inside `$reactiveRoot`? Actually we can: the value of $reactiveRoot can be a string reference — "The value is either literal data, or a string reference, in which case the root is bound to the referenced site." So `$reactiveRoot: "{self}.closest"` would bind to the closest object. Not what we want. Simpler: define the umbrella with the `closest` finder logic inherited, let imageGenerator's members operate on `state.prompt`, and add an effect or method: when the user clicks a button... Actually the user's requirement: "move it close to a sticky note and press a button to generate an image". The note text should become the prompt. Options: 1. The visible input displays the closest note's text and is bound as the prompt (read-only). Generate button searches Pixabay with it. 2. The input shows an editable prompt, and "Generate" first adopts the closest note's text. The cleanest reading: moving near a note sets what the widget generates from; press the button → image of that note. I'll wire `state.prompt` to track `noteText` via an `$effect`? Or better: define prompt as a `$compute` and override the input binding's site... but the subcomponents `errorMessage`/`result`/`loadingMessage` reference `{imageGenerator}.image` etc. — using nickname resolution. In the merged umbrella they'd resolve from self: `{self}.image` works since umbrella has `image` member. But hold on — maybe simplest robust approach: rather than a big merged layer, create the composition with subcomponents and cross-injection as the hint describes: ```js fluid.def("fluid.demos.noteToImage", { $layers: ["fluid.topLevelWidget"], finder: { $component: { $layers: "fluid.demos.closestNoteFinder" } }, generator: { $component: { $layers: "fluid.demos.imageGenerator", state: { prompt: "{finder}.noteText" } } }, view: "{generator}.view" }); ``` Problem: `state: {prompt: "..."}` — but state is a `$reactiveRoot`; overriding a single member... In the subcomponent layer for `generator`, `state` would be a partial? The `state` key in the `$component` record replaces `state`? Then state would lose isGenerating etc. Not good. Per IL merging: "Any other value (primitive, array, function, signal record) from a stronger layer replaces that from a weaker one wholesale." And `state` is a signal record `{$reactiveRoot: {...}}`. So overriding `state` wholesale replaces the whole reactive root. To only override prompt, we'd need `state: {$reactiveRoot: {prompt: "{finder}.noteText"}}` — but then isGenerating etc. are missing... Do they get picked up? No. Hmm, what about `prompt` handling inside the generator component: maybe define the overlay at a different level. Actually maybe we should treat the `state` override differently: give generator's `state` the full record with prompt referencing the finder: The `generate` method of imageGenerator uses `state.prompt.trim()`. So if we could set prompt to noteText, everything works, including the displayed error flow. The input `value="@{state.prompt}"` shows it, writable but it's from the note text — actually if the input is bound two-way to `state.prompt` inside the generator component... wait in the generator's SFC template, `@{state.prompt}` resolves against the generator component's state. If generator's `state.prompt` were `"{finder}.noteText"` (sited reference), writing from the input would write through to `closest.text`... which is a `$compute` — read-only, writes rejected/re-materialised. And `noteText` = "A red fox in the snow" always readable. OK. But constructing `state` with prompt referencing finder while keeping other fields requires the umbrella to fully specify state. But wait — in the `$component` record for `generator`, the `state` key: the generator's layer already defines `state: {$reactiveRoot: {prompt: "", isGenerating: false, ...}}`. If the subcomponent record specifies `state` partially `{$reactiveRoot: {prompt: ...}}`... it replaces the whole record. Missing keys → prompt present, others absent → generator breaks. Alternative: the umbrella computes `state.prompt` via `$compute` that reads noteText, then... no, can't mix into $reactiveRoot. Different approach: change the prompt source used by generate/cannotGenerate, i.e., override `prompt` member? The generator doesn't have a `prompt` member; it uses `state.prompt`. We could override `generate`/`cannotGenerate`... hmm but generate is `$method` with args `["{self}.state"]` calling `fluid.demos.imageGenerator.generate(state)`. The function reads `state.prompt`. If umbrella overrides `state`... same problem. OK here's another thought: the umbrella simply creates `state` itself? No... Alternative cleaner: keep the two component subcomponents separate, and give the generator its own state with prompt bound through an effect from finder: In the umbrella: ```js finder: { $component: { $layers: "fluid.demos.closestNoteFinder" } }, generator: { $component: { $layers: "fluid.demos.imageGenerator" } }, ``` and sync prompt: `"$effect: ..."` — but $effect writes produce source "il"? Writing `generator.state.prompt = finder.noteText` on every note/position change. But generate's "Ignore generate request while generation is in progress" check and such would still work. But there's an undo concern... The tldraw clipboard handles undo; effect writes happen outside user actions... it would cause state churn. Eh. Actually, wait. Let me reconsider the merged-parent-layers approach with custom view. The umbrella: ```js fluid.def("fluid.demos.noteImageGenerator", { $layers: ["fluid.demos.closestNoteFinder", "fluid.demos.imageGenerator", "fluid.topLevelWidget"], preferredSize: {w: 400, h: 660}, ... }); ``` Members inherited: finder's `closest`, `noteText`, `distance`, `distanceLine`(subcomponent), imageGenerator's everything, including `state`, computed members, methods, subcomponents. Conflicts: `preferredSize` (override own), `view` (override own — needed anyway since neither parent view fits). Now, the template (via `fluid.templateViewComponent`, since SFC not needed): ```html
@{noteText}
Distance @{distance}px (hidden when null)
{ if (state.prompt !== noteText && noteText) state.prompt = noteText; }, args: ["{self}.state", "{self}.noteText"] } } ``` Hmm — if noteText is "Not placed on a canvas", prompt becomes that; search would fail harmlessly. Fine; or skip empty. noteText is never empty string. OK just assign unconditionally. But there's a subtlety: writing state.prompt triggers re-render of the input (bound to state.prompt) — displays note text. Also if the user could edit prompt... we won't give them an editable input; read-only via template binding to noteText might cause write-back attempts on read-only compute → re-materialised from element state; okay but let me instead bind the input to `{self}.state.prompt`... but then effect will overwrite any typing. Hmm. Do we want typing allowed? The concept: "move it close to a sticky note and press a button to generate an image" — the note provides the prompt. I'll make the input read-only showing the note text, and disable editing while generating (inherited disabled attr). Simplest: show the note text in a read-only input styled like the generator's: `value="@{state.prompt}" readonly`. Write-back from user input would write to state.prompt, then effect overwrites on next stabilize (since noteText triggers only when changed; typing changes state.prompt but not noteText — effect depends on [state, noteText]... state.prompt is part of `state` reference which is the whole reactive root → effect reruns when any field changes, overwriting the typed char. Ugh. Use args `["{self}.state.prompt"...]` no. Filter: effect args could be `["{self}.state.isGenerating", "{self}.noteText"]` — wait exclude source "dom"? Then user typing (dom source) still changes state.prompt but effect wouldn't rerun because its dependencies are isGenerating and noteText only. Nice: ```js syncPrompt: { $effect: { func: (isGenerating, noteText) => { ... }, args: ["{self}.state.isGenerating", "{self}.noteText"] } } ``` But func needs state to write. Can write via closure? No — $effect func args are signals only. We can reference self via global? Functions must be global or referenced. Pass whole state but excludeSource "dom": ```js syncPrompt: { $effect: { func: "fluid.demos.noteImageGenerator.syncPrompt", args: ["{self}.state", "{self}.noteText"], excludeSource: "dom" } } ``` with `fluid.demos.noteImageGenerator.syncPrompt = (state, noteText) => { if (state.prompt !== noteText) state.prompt = noteText; }`. User typing creates dom-sourced update → excluded → their text... but effect reruns also on dom writes? excludeSource means the effect is not notified of dom updates at all; but state.prompt update by typing is dom; effect skips; so the typed text persists (and the effect's own writes are il/whatever source, included). But wait — when generation completes, isGenerating flips (il writes from generate method → included), effect reruns, prompt reset from note. Acceptable. Hmm, but actually hold on — is this overengineering? Maybe simply: input is `readonly` and bound to `@{noteText}` directly. Writing to `noteText` — it's `{self}.closest.text`, closest being `$compute` — read-only; template binding re-materialises from element state (per docs: "Read-only sources. If the site holds a computed value ($compute), it is not written. The attribute is re-materialised from the element's state"). And `cannotGenerate` uses `state.prompt`... The cleanest is the effect sync. Let me just do the effect sync with excludeSource "dom". Then `cannotGenerate` (uses state.prompt) works; generate works. Edge: While `isGenerating` true, prompt frozen — but note moves during generation; after finishing, effect reruns (isGenerating changed) and syncs. Good. Now the template. Combined layout: finder header (title, note text, distance) + generator body (input, buttons, messages, result). Use the classes from the two SFCs (both injected): `notefinder-title`, `notefinder-text`, `notefinder-distance`, `imagegen`, `imagegen-title`, `imagegen-input`, `imagegen-buttons`, `imagegen-button`, `imagegen-another`, plus container classes. My custom template must supply its own sizing; the SFC styles target `.notefinder { padding... height:100% }` etc. If my root mirrors both, I can compose: root div class maybe "noteimagegen" with styles of my own (I control them since umbrella is new layer). But careful: imagegen-related CSS rules (.imagegen {display flex; flex-direction column; height 100%}) only apply if the elements have those classes names. If I use the same class names on my elements, the existing injected CSS applies — no new styles needed! But do those SFC styles actually exist in the workspace?
